title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to Grothendieck's motivic and standard-conjectures circle of notes on algebraic cycles on abelian varieties. The neighbouring pages are an unrelated typescript on topos cohomology, probably by a student, filed in the same folder.

(1) A homomorphism u: A -> B of abelian varieties is determined by the cohomology class of its graph Gamma_u in A x B. Grothendieck adds that here the class is only really known in l-adic cohomology. The reason is that from the class one recovers the induced map on cohomology, i.e. V_l(u) = T_l(u) tensor Q_l. The map Hom(A,B) -> Hom(T_l A, T_l B) is injective, so this map determines u. Grothendieck phrases it as: 'one knows the graph, hence V_l(Gamma) inside V_l(A x B)'.

(2) Likewise an abelian subvariety C of A is determined by its class. In modern terms, the class of C in H^{2(g-d)} corresponds to a decomposable line in Lambda^{2d} V_l(A), which pins down the subspace V_l(C) and hence C.

(3) He recalls the classical theory of divisorial correspondences (Weil, Lang): the codimension-1 cycle classes satisfy C^1(A x B)/(C^1(A) + C^1(B)) = Hom(A, B*), where B* is the dual abelian variety. He calls its cohomological meaning 'clear' via Kunneth:
- H^2(A x B)(1) = Lambda^2(H^1 A + H^1 B)(1);
- modulo Lambda^2 H^1(A)(1) + Lambda^2 H^1(B)(1), this leaves H^1(A) tensor H^1(B)(1);
- the latter is isomorphic to Hom(T_l A, T_l B*), using H^1(A) = T_l(A)^dual and H^1(B)(1) = T_l(B*) via the Weil pairing.

(4) The page ends with an unfinished 'Question': prove that for an element of H^1(A) tensor H^1(B)(1), inside H^2(A x B)(1), to be algebraic [it is necessary and sufficient that ...]. The natural completion is: iff it lies in the image of Hom(A,B*) tensor Q_l. Over a finitely generated base field this means iff it is Galois-invariant. That is the Tate conjecture for divisors on A x B, equivalently Tate's isogeny conjecture Hom(A,B*) tensor Z_l = Hom_Gal(T_l A, T_l B*). Tate proved it over finite fields in 1966, Zarhin in positive-characteristic function fields, and Faltings over number fields in 1983. Alternatively, over C, the completion is the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem for abelian varieties.
errors: He writes the Cartesian product 'x' where direct sums '+' of cohomology groups (and of the C^1 subgroups) are meant.

The argument 'one knows the class, hence one knows the graph, hence V_l(Gamma)' is stated loosely. The rigorous version is that the class gives V_l(u), and V_l(u) determines u by injectivity of Hom(A,B) tensor Z_l -> Hom(T_l A, T_l B). This is correct but compressed.

ideas.what: Homomorphisms and abelian subvarieties are determined by their l-adic cohomology classes
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of Hom(A,B) tensor Z_l -> Hom(T_l A, T_l B); faithfulness of the realization on abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Classical (Weil, Lang 'Abelian varieties', Mumford); not specific to Grothendieck

ideas.what: Divisorial correspondences C^1(AxB)/(C^1A+C^1B) = Hom(A,B*), together with its Kunneth interpretation as H^1(A) tensor H^1(B)(1) = Hom(T_l A, T_l B*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang; the cohomological form is standard (Tate 1966, Mumford)
ideas.where_published: Standard (Lang, Mumford 'Abelian Varieties'); not specifically in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Question: characterize the algebraic classes in H^1(A) tensor H^1(B)(1)
ideas.modern_name: Tate conjecture for divisors on A x B, equivalently Tate's isogeny conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (conjecture 1963/64, proof over finite fields 1966); Zarhin (1975); Faltings (1983)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck discusses the Tate conjecture in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and in correspondence; this specific question is not known there

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material on divisorial correspondences and their l-adic interpretation, plus an unfinished question that is exactly Tate's conjecture for abelian varieties. Tate formulated it around the same time and it was later proved (Tate, Zarhin, Faltings). This is historically interesting as evidence that Grothendieck was thinking about it, but it is not new.
transcription_corrections: Line 4-5: the struck-out words are followed by '(ici on ne la connait au fond que dans la cohomologie l-adique)'. The transcribed 'coh. cohomologique' is a misreading.
The subscripts in T_{Q_l}(Gamma) subset T_{Q_l}(A x B) are Q_l, i.e. V_l in modern notation.
The symbol below H^1(A) tensor H^1(B)(1), transcribed '∪ [?]', is a vertical isomorphism sign (≀), relating it to Hom(T_l(A), T_l(B*)).
In the quotients, 'x' between the C^1 groups and between the Lambda^2 terms denotes direct sum.
